title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - Pinecrest Health
summary: POC scoping call to align on private networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency constraints for EU/Canada, workload sizing and benchmarks, and POC timeline. Customer requires on-prem-style isolation and audit logs; agreed next steps include security pack, test account, and benchmark run within two weeks.
action_items: Samir Patel: Share Private Networking whitepaper and security pack (SOC2 + network diagrams) - due 2026-12-22
Lucas Chen: Provision test VPC peering endpoints and sample benchmark harness credentials - due 2026-12-27
Anika Ruiz / Pinecrest: Share current network CIDR blocks, proxy egress IPs and list of allowed regions - due 2026-12-23
Ben Roberts: Confirm data residency policy for PHI and whether audit log retention needs to be 7 years - due 2026-12-29
next_steps: Samir to send security docs + network diagram link
Lucas to schedule walkthrough of benchmark harness and run initial 2-hour latency/throughput test next week
Customer to provide network CIDRs and internal PO to start pilot once POC results are satisfactory
Schedule a follow-up technical deep dive with Pinecrest infra team on 2026-12-28
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-20 10:00 PST | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (CTO - Pinecrest), Anika Ruiz (Head of Infra), Ben Roberts (Security)

Summary: quick scoping for Private networking POC, focusing on VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink, regions (EU + CA), egress controls and benchmark plan.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we, uh, appreciate the time. Quick round robin - Lucas is our solutions engineer, he'll drive the benchmark and tech bits.
[00:12] Dr. Maya Singh: Thanks Samir. We're trying to validate Redwood Private for patient-facing NLP services. Key point is we need all inference traffic to stay within region and, um, meet our egress/whitelisting rules.
[00:28] Lucas: Got it. Quick clarifying q, when you say "stay within region" do you mean compute + response storage and logs, or just the model compute?
[00:37] Anika: Ideally both. Compute in EU region (Frankfurt) for EU patients, Canada region for CA patients. Logs and artifacts need to be stored in those regions as well. No cross-region replication unless explicitly allowed.
[00:50] Ben: And auditability — we need audit logs shipped to our SIEM, and ability to rotate KMS keys from our vault.
[00:58] Samir: That's doable — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit export. We'll share the SOC2 and network diagrams. Note: sometimes the transcription or internal docs call it "Redwood Privet" — ignore that, it is Redwood Private.
[01:10] Lucas: For network topology there are two common patterns we've seen: VPC peering (classic) or AWS PrivateLink / Private Service Connect depending on cloud. VPC peering is simpler but requires route management; PrivateLink gives you interface endpoints which are better for tight egress controls.
[01:27] Dr. Maya Singh: Are there tradeoffs for latency? We care about 99th percentile latency — our SLA target is < 200ms on inference for short prompts.
[01:36] Lucas: PrivateLink adds a small extra hop but in practice it's sub 10ms for intra-region. Biggest latency factors are model selection, tokenization and batch sizes. For POC we'll need to run our benchmark on your expected prompt distribution.
[01:48] Anika: For workload sizing, here's what we are seeing: peak concurrency ~150 concurrent sessions, average request is 120 tokens in, 80 tokens out, about 250 requests per second during peak windows. But this is pre-alpha, so numbers could swing.
[02:05] Samir: Perfect. For scoping the POC we'll assume 250 RPS and provision a small dedicated pool that simulates 200-300 RPS. Success criteria, does this alignment look right: 99th latency < 200ms for standard prompts, throughput >= 200 RPS sustained for 15m, no request failures, and audit logs delivered to your SIEM within 5 minutes?
[02:24] Ben: Yes, and in addition we want connection endpoints to be pinned — static egress IPs or NATs we can whitelist. We can't accept dynamic, ephemeral egress.
[02:34] Lucas: We can provide egress IPs from the dedicated Redwood Private connectors, or you can set up VPC peering and use your NAT. We'll list the IP ranges. For PrivateLink, you still need to accept interface endpoints on your side; egress wise, the traffic stays in your VPC until it hits our service endpoint.
[02:49] Dr. Maya Singh: Are there any limitations with Platform features like streaming and function calling when using Private networking?
[02:56] Lucas: Streaming works fine over PrivateLink/VPC peering. Function calling is a higher-level SDK feature and operates the same; just need to allow the required ports (HTTPS) and we'll provide end-to-end tests.
[03:07] Samir: On data residency, we also need to clarify retention defaults. We offer configurable retention; for Private deployments you can opt to disable logs or set retention to customer policy. We'll add that to the security doc.
[03:18] Anika: For the benchmark, we'd like to run both latency and throughput tests. Can you give a sample harness? We want to run it inside our staging VPC to simulate correct network path.
[03:27] Lucas: Yes — we have a Jenkins-style harness and a k6 load script we can drop into your infra. We'll need a small set of credentials and a test API endpoint (provisioned via PrivateLink or peering). We'll also provide a sample dataset of 1,500 prompts that match the clinical DSL you described.
[03:41] Ben: One security nuance — PHI flows. We need to ensure TLS termination is customer-controlled or meet mutual TLS requirements for egress. Is mTLS possible?
[03:50] Samir: We support mTLS for PrivateLink endpoints and can negotiate cert rotation with your infosec. We'll document the exact cipher suites.
[03:58] Dr. Maya Singh: Timeline? We want POC results and a recommendation by mid-Jan. Can we do that?
[04:04] Samir: Yes. Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) — exchange network diagrams and security pack; Week 1 — provision PrivateLink endpoints or peering and run initial connectivity tests; Week 2 — run full benchmark (24-48 hours of varied load tests); Week 3 — analyze results and present findings. That lands analysis around 2027-01-10 to 2027-01-14.
[04:23] Anika: That works for us, assuming the provisioning can happen over next 3 business days. We need the IP ranges and any ASN/cidr to prep the firewall rules.
[04:31] Lucas: We'll include the CIDR, egress IPs and exact ports in the network diagram. Also note: if you prefer VPC peering we need to coordinate route table updates — peering can be setup in parallel and tested within 24 hours usually. PrivateLink requires creating interface endpoints on your side — also ~24-48h including security reviews.
[04:49] Ben: For audit logs, can we push logs to our s3 bucket or do you prefer pushing to our SIEM? We prefer direct S3 delivery with encryption using our KMS.
[04:58] Samir: We can push to your S3 (server-side encryption with customer KMS). We'll include the S3 bucket policy example.
[05:04] Dr. Maya Singh: For success criteria, add also regression tests on output quality — we need to ensure quantization or batching doesn't degrade clinical extraction accuracy by >2% on our eval set.
[05:15] Lucas: Good call. We'll run an automated eval against your golden set and measure F1/accuracy. We'll include that as pass/fail in the POC report.
[05:24] Samir: Ok recap: deliverables from Redwood: security pack (SOC2 + KMS+network diagrams), benchmark harness and sample prompts, test endpoints (PrivateLink or VPC peering), static egress IP ranges, and an eval script for quality regression. Deliverables from Pinecrest: network CIDRs, SIEM/S3 destinations, decision on PrivateLink vs peering, and PO if moving to pilot.
[05:44] Anika: We'll try to get the CIDRs and decision by 2026-12-23.
[05:49] Ben: Quick question: any limitations on model variants in Private mode? We use some Llama-derived models internally.
[05:56] Lucas: We can host a variety of open models; for Private deployments we'll validate the model runtime and quantization profile. Some very-large models may need multiple GPUs and will affect latency. We'll call that out in the sizing doc.
[06:10] Dr. Maya Singh: Great. Last thing — cost expectations. High level only for now.
[06:15] Samir: For the POC we'll cover minimal infra; for production we'll propose a dedicated pool priced by reserved capacity. We'll share a rough estimate after the benchmark.
[06:22] Dr. Maya Singh: OK thanks everyone.
[06:26] Samir: Thanks — next steps in the chat, I'll send the security link and schedule the tech deep dive for 2026-12-28.

Artifacts shared: https://redwood.example.com/soc2-pkg, https://redwood.example.com/private-networking-diagram.pdf, https://redwood.example.com/benchmark-harness-k6.tar.gz

Notes on transcription: may include minor mis-hearings (Redwood Privet vs Private, firewall CDR vs CIDR, etc.), filler words preserved.

End of transcript.
